<details>
<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

This PR fixes duplicate relabel series produced when pods are owned through a ReplicationController chain created by a DeploymentConfig. The fix modifies the `namespace_workload_pod:kube_pod_owner:relabel` recording rule to exclude `owner_kind="ReplicationController"` from its kube_pod_owner selector. A corresponding jsonnet sanitization patch is added to apply the same modification during rule generation, and a new test case validates that pods in such chains produce exactly one series with `workload_type="deploymentconfig"` rather than duplicates.

> It may useful for upstream to allow the customization of non-standard types?
> 
> Instead of
> 
> ```
>  kube_pod_owner{
> job="kube-state-metrics", 
> owner_kind!="ReplicaSet", owner_kind!="ReplicationController", owner_kind!="DaemonSet", owner_kind!="StatefulSet", owner_kind!="Job", owner_kind!="Node", owner_kind!=""}
> ```
> 
> we could have
> 
> ```
>  kube_pod_owner{
> job="kube-state-metrics", 
> owner_kind!~"ReplicaSet|ReplicationController|DaemonSet|StatefulSet|Job|Node|"}
> ```

Good point, thanks Simon. Agreed on both counts.

I'll update the PR and also open a PR upstream at kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin to propose making the excluded owner kinds configurable, so distributions that add custom owner kind rules (like our DeploymentConfig one) can extend the exclusion list without patching.

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-monitoring-operator/pull/2932):

>When a `DeploymentConfig` is used, the pod ownership chain is `DeploymentConfig → ReplicationController → Pod`. Two recording rules both produce a `namespace_workload_pod:kube_pod_owner:relabel` series for the same `(namespace, pod)`:
>1. Our custom DeploymentConfig rule walks from `ReplicationController` to `DeploymentConfig` via `kube_replicationcontroller_owner` and emits `workload_type=deploymentconfig`.
>2. The upstream catch-all rule (from kubernetes-mixin) matches any `owner_kind` not explicitly excluded. It excludes `ReplicaSet`, `DaemonSet`, `StatefulSet`, `Job`, and `Node` — but not `ReplicationController`. So it also fires and emits `workload_type=ReplicationController`.
>Dashboard queries that join on `(namespace, pod)` with `group_left` then fail with: `many-to-many matching not allowed: matching labels must be unique on one side`.
>Reproduced on 4.21.0-0.nightly-2026-05-24-163444.
>
>## Fix
>Exclude `owner_kind=ReplicationController` from the upstream catch-all rule via the existing `patchedRules` mechanism in `sanitize-rules.libsonnet`, so that only our custom DeploymentConfig rule produces the recording rule result for these pods.
>
>## Testing
>- Added `test/rules/OCPBUGS-86352.yaml` — promtool unit test simulating a DeploymentConfig pod, asserting exactly one series per `(namespace, pod)` with `workload_type=deploymentconfig`.
>- Full `make test-rules` passes with no regressions.
>- Verified fix on a live 4.21 cluster: before the fix, 2 series per pod; after, only 1.
>
>

If you have questions or suggestions related to my behavior, please file an issue against the [openshift-eng/jira-lifecycle-plugin](https://github.com/openshift-eng/jira-lifecycle-plugin/issues/new) repository.

🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
jsonnet/utils/sanitize-rules.libsonnet (1)
`485-502`: _💤 Low value_ **Patch correctly excludes ReplicationController from catch-all rule.** The `std.strReplace` approach successfully inserts `owner_kind!="ReplicationController"` into the exclusion filter, preventing duplicate series for DeploymentConfig-owned pods. The comment clearly documents the purpose and references OCPBUGS-86352. The string replacement is somewhat fragile—if upstream reformats the expression or reorders the exclusions, the replacement will silently fail. However, this pattern is consistent with other patches in this file and any failure would likely be caught by the new test in `test/rules/OCPBUGS-86352.yaml`.
🔍 Optional: Add verification for replacement success Consider adding an assertion to verify the replacement succeeded: ```diff expr: function(expr) - std.strReplace( + local result = std.strReplace( expr, 'owner_kind!="ReplicaSet", owner_kind!="DaemonSet"', 'owner_kind!="ReplicaSet", owner_kind!="ReplicationController", owner_kind!="DaemonSet"', - ), + ); + assert result != expr : 'OCPBUGS-86352 patch failed - upstream expression format may have changed'; + result, ``` This would make the build fail explicitly if the upstream format changes, rather than silently producing incorrect rules.
